A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LEXam and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–G. Text and visual inspection support comparison of the figures, tables and mathematical content. All appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on legal questions, MCQ perturbation experiments, and human-expert validation of LLM judges in Tables 2–4 and Appendices C, D and G.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports MCQ accuracy grouped by affirmative versus negative question wording in Figure 4E.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, MCQ generation, answering prompts and the GPT-4o judging procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix E. The polarity label and subgroup analysis do not change model inference or scoring.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 2,841 open questions, 1,660 main MCQs and 385 auxiliary MCQs, with the same languages, legal domains and jurisdictions. The polarity analysis groups existing questions without adding a dataset or a generated rephrasing scenario.

E2.justification: The 19 evaluated models in Table 2, seven models in Table 3, and LLM-judge and constant-score comparisons in Appendix G are unchanged. Figure 4E uses the existing reasoning, large and small model groups.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, prompts, inference settings, the 4/8/16/32-choice perturbation protocol and expert-evaluation design remain unchanged. The added polarity breakdown does not document revised inputs, model settings or a controlled rephrasing experiment.

E4.justification: Figure 4E adds a targeted analysis comparing affirmative and negative MCQs. This differs from the retained analysis of whether answer choices include 'none of the statements' in Appendix C.2. Existing perturbation and supplementary analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The polarity panel uses the existing bootstrapped-standard-error practice. Three-sample judge-variability reporting and the expert-agreement and alt-test procedures are unchanged; no additional runs, seeds or statistical testing procedure are reported.

E6.justification: Figure 4E newly reports lower accuracy on negative questions across all three model groups, with the largest gap for reasoning models and small-model accuracy near 25% chance. Existing table results, rankings and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and thresholds of the Alternative Annotator Test remain unchanged. The polarity label is an operational metadata description, with no new formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about challenging legal reasoning, differentiating model capabilities and validating scalable LLM-based evaluation. The polarity analysis adds supporting detail without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets the polarity gap as sensitivity to negative phrasing and calls the larger penalty for reasoning models counterintuitive. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning jurisdictional coverage, languages and changing laws remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly documents the negative_question metadata field, including an example of negative wording. This helps identify the new analysis groups. Prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, costs, annotation instructions and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and dataset comparison in Table 1 are unchanged. Reference pagination shifts, but research positioning and novelty claims are retained.

P1.justification: v3 locally revises the metadata paragraph and MCQ-results discussion, changes metadata naming conventions and adds acknowledgments. It also removes embedded AI-reviewer-directed text after the references. The broader narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn from four to five panels, adding polarity axes, a legend and an updated caption. Nearby text and tables reflow, while other figures, table structures and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the documented polarity breakdown in Section 3.2 and Figure 4E provides a useful additional diagnostic of model weaknesses while preserving the main experimental evidence. The benefit is limited: comparing existing question subsets without a matched rephrasing control does not establish that polarity itself causes the accuracy gap.
